caption: Rovo agents can change Jira for you. That is the scary part.
say: Rovo agents can now change Jira for you. That is also the scary part. One confident agent can close a customer escalation, or touch a security ticket, in seconds.

caption: Warden: a policy firewall for Rovo agents. The model proposes. Plain code decides.
say: Warden is a policy firewall for Rovo agents. The model proposes. Plain code decides. No language model is ever asked whether a change is allowed.

scene: Mandate tab, scroll through rules and limits
caption: The admin writes a mandate: scope, hard rules, sensitive rules, limits, expiry.
say: An admin writes a mandate. Which projects and actions the agent may touch. Labels it must never touch. Labels that need a person first. And limits per run, per hour and per day, on rolling windows.

scene: Rovo chat: Move PAY-8 to In Progress, confirm, Cleared receipt
caption: A safe change: Warden reads the facts from Jira, not from the agent. Cleared.
say: Let's ask the Triage Steward agent to move PAY-8 to In Progress. Warden reads the facts from Jira itself, not from what the agent claims. Inside the mandate, so it is cleared, and done.

scene: Rovo chat: Move PAY-7 and PAY-4 to Done, Refused and Hold
caption: Security work is refused. Release-critical work waits for a person.
say: Now two riskier ones. PAY-7 carries the security label, so it is refused, and the agent is told not to retry. PAY-4 is release-critical, so it is held for a person. Nothing has been written.

scene: Rovo chat: user insists, agent still refused
caption: Insisting does not help. Warden is the only path to a write.
say: What if the user insists, or an issue description tries to talk the agent into it? It does not matter. Warden is the only path to a write, and the rule is code.

scene: Rovo chat: Move PAY-2 to In Progress, Hold for protected goal
caption: Teamwork Graph: PAY-2 is linked to a protected company goal, so it waits.
say: Labels are not the whole story. PAY-2 looks harmless, but the Teamwork Graph shows it is linked to the company's revenue goal, which this mandate protects. So it waits for a person. If the graph cannot be reached, Warden holds instead of guessing.

scene: Warden Approvals: PAY-5 receipt, Approve and apply
caption: Held changes wait as a receipt. Approval re-checks the issue and the rules first.
say: Held changes wait here as a receipt: the exact change, why it was held, and the mandate version. When I approve, Warden re-reads the issue and re-checks the current rules first. A refusal always beats an approval.

scene: Simulator: project = PAY, move to Done
caption: Simulate a bulk run before anything happens. Nothing is written.
say: Before a bulk run, simulate it. Every issue in the project, judged in a second, with the reason for each verdict. Limits are projected across the whole plan, so a big run is stopped up front, not halfway.

caption: Every decision lands in the ledger, exportable for audit.
say: Every decision lands in the ledger: the request, the verdict, the rule, and what happened next. One click exports it for your auditors.

scene: Closing card: Rovo agent, MCP, Teamwork Graph, tests
caption: Warden. Let agents work, without handing them the keys.
say: The same guarded tools are exposed over MCP, so any agent gets the same guardrails. Warden. Let agents work, without handing them the keys.
